label: START F5
title: Osmotic laxative for long-term constipation
statement: Osmotic laxative (e.g., lactulose, macrogol, sorbitol) for chronic persistent idiopathic or secondary benign constipation.

source.document: O'Mahony D, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632, Appendix 1 (corrected supplementary file; NHS Somerset copy used for text, sentence-identical to the earlier parse)
source.citation: O'Mahony D, Cherubini A, Guiteras AR, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632. doi:10.1007/s41999-023-00777-y
source.credit: O'Mahony D, Cherubini A, Guiteras AR, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632. doi:10.1007/s41999-023-00777-y

plain_summary: A person with constipation that keeps coming back, with no serious cause, should usually take an osmotic laxative, which draws water into the bowel to soften the stool.

needs_facts.meets: Persistent or recurrent constipation is present. A single short episode does not qualify.
A clinical assessment establishes an idiopathic or secondary benign cause. A serious cause excludes the omission. If the cause is uncertain, leave it unresolved.

options.words: Idiopathic or secondary benign cause established

medicine_groups.name: Osmotic laxatives (medicines that meet this criterion)
medicine_groups.note: Macrogol packs with electrolytes count. Stimulant laxatives such as senna and bisacodyl, stool softeners such as docusate, and fibre supplements do not count. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too. Exclude macrogol bowel-cleansing preparations used for a procedure.

medicine_groups.name: Medicines that imply the condition
medicine_groups.note: Repeated supply of a stimulant laxative or stool softener, at least three supplies in six months, suggests long-term constipation. One or two supplies do not. Count only oral or rectal laxative forms. Exclude docusate ear drops, even when the brand name resembles that of an oral laxative.

rule_for_models: Apply this criterion only to people aged 65 years or older. If age is unknown, confirm it before reporting a finding. Give no finding for a qualifying Group A supply in the last six months counted back from the latest date in the record, a short episode, a serious cause, a valid reason to omit treatment including a contraindication, or end-of-life care with a palliative focus. Exclude macrogol bowel preparations for a procedure from Group A. With no Group A osmotic laxative in that six-month window, report a finding only if the record shows both persistent or recurrent constipation and an assessed idiopathic or secondary benign cause. A single diagnosis or earlier combined answer may establish both. Use an earlier answer only for what it records. When duration or cause is unknown, report only a possible finding if the rest of the evidence fits. Name Chronic constipation for missing chronicity and Assessed cause of chronic constipation for a missing cause. If neither is recorded, name both. With no constipation line, report a possible finding only if at least three Group B oral or rectal laxative supplies fall in the same six months. Exclude docusate ear drops. Cite the evidence for chronicity and cause when present, or the three qualifying supplies when these alone trigger review.
cannot_be_seen: Why the person uses a stimulant laxative, how long the constipation has lasted, and whether a bowel blockage or another serious cause has been ruled out. Laxatives or iron bought without a dispensing label and medicines supplied elsewhere may be missing. A local opioid or iron supply is visible, but the supply alone does not establish the cause.
ask_the_gp: Whether an osmotic laxative would suit this person, and whether the cause of the constipation has been looked for.
